blocks.text: 1. Code Assistant
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061584-347188000.png

Customer Support Bot closed by pointing toward a research assistant for open-ended research across a huge, uncurated corpus. Code Assistant, a RAG system design for grounding answers in an actual codebase, applies the same retrieval and generation discipline to source code instead of documents.
It retrieves relevant functions, files, and documentation rather than relying on generic programming knowledge.
2. The Design Problem's Scope
A developer asks questions about a specific, real codebase, not general programming concepts.
The knowledge base is the codebase itself, not documents about code.

blocks.text: 3. Chunking Code By Semantic Units, Not Fixed Lines

blocks.alt: Chunking Code By Semantic Units, Not Fixed Lines
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061584-299792554.png
As with the fixed chunking versus recursive chunking comparison in Chunking, splitting code at an arbitrary line count can cut a function or class in half.
Chunking by function, class, or module boundary keeps each chunk semantically complete.
4. Retrieving Across Files For Cross-Referenced Code

blocks.alt: Retrieving Across Files For Cross-Referenced Code
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061934-293065354.png
Similar to the hidden dependency chains covered in Multi-Hop RAG, a function's behavior often depends on another function defined in a completely different file.
Following an import or a function call means retrieval must span multiple files, not just one.
5. Keyword Search For Exact Identifiers
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061935-562705826.png
As with hybrid search covered in Retrieval, a developer asking about a specific function name needs exact keyword matching, not fuzzy semantic similarity.
Combining keyword and semantic search serves both precise lookups and vague conceptual questions.

blocks.text: 6. Keeping The Index Current With Every Commit

blocks.alt: Keeping The Index Current With Every Commit
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061935-471840100.png
As Real-Time Updates covers, code changes with every commit, far more frequently than most other knowledge bases.
Incremental indexing triggered by the version control system keeps retrieval accurate.
7. Generating Code With Cited Source Locations

blocks.alt: Generating Code With Cited Source Locations
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061935-841072470.png
Following the citation format consistency covered in Citation Prompting, a generated code suggestion should cite the specific file and function it was grounded in.
A developer can verify the suggestion against the actual source it was drawn from.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A code suggestion citing utils/auth.py, line 42, lets a developer immediately jump to the referenced function and verify the suggestion is actually consistent with it.

blocks.text: 8. Faithfulness Matters More For Code Than Prose
As Faithfulness establishes, faithfulness does not check factual accuracy, but a hallucinated function signature or a nonexistent method fails immediately when the code actually runs.
Code generation has a stricter, more immediate correctness check than prose ever does.
9. Recognizing When This Code Assistant Design Fits The Actual Need

blocks.alt: Recognizing When This Code Assistant Design Fits The Actual Need
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448061935-174781384.png
A developer needing answers grounded in a real, specific codebase fits this design.
General programming questions with no specific codebase need no retrieval at all.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates function-level chunking, keyword lookup, and a cited code suggestion.

code.content:
code_chunks = [
    {"file": "utils/auth.py", "function": "verify_token", "text": "def verify_token(token): return jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY)"},
    {"file": "utils/auth.py", "function": "hash_password", "text": "def hash_password(password): return bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), salt)"},
    {"file": "models/user.py", "function": "get_user_by_id", "text": "def get_user_by_id(user_id): return User.query.get(user_id)"},
]

def keyword_search(query, chunks):
    # exact identifier lookup via keyword matching
    return [c for c in chunks if query.lower() in c["function"].lower()]

def generate_with_citation(query, retrieved):
    # citation includes the source file and function
    if not retrieved:
        return "No matching function found in the codebase."
    top = retrieved[0]
    return f"{top['text']}\n# Source: {top['file']}, function {top['function']}"

print("Code assistant example:")
results = keyword_search("verify_token", code_chunks)
print(generate_with_citation("verify_token", results))

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the exact function retrieved by name with a source citation appended.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Chunking code at a fixed line count instead of at function or class boundaries.
Retrieving from only the current file when the relevant logic lives in a cross-referenced file.
Relying on semantic search alone for queries asking about a specific, exact function name.
Letting the code index go stale after commits instead of updating it incrementally.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: A code assistant grounds answers in an actual, specific codebase, not general programming knowledge.
The knowledge base is the codebase itself, not documents describing code.
Chunking by function, class, or module boundary keeps each chunk semantically complete.
A function's behavior often depends on code in another file, requiring retrieval to span files.
Combining keyword and semantic search serves both exact identifier lookups and conceptual questions.
Code changes with every commit, requiring incremental indexing tied to version control.
Citing the specific file and function a suggestion was grounded in lets a developer verify it.
A hallucinated function signature fails immediately when code runs, a stricter check than prose gets.
